worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit by simply evaluating the function at $x=0$, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+1}-1} & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{0+1}-1}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+1}-1} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{(\sqrt{x+1}-1)(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{(\sqrt{x+1})^{2}-{1}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{(x+1)-1} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\cancel{x}(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{\cancel{x}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\sqrt{x+1}+1) \\  & =\sqrt{0+1}+1 \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
